Effect and Cause
A chance finding by a Swiss research team explains an event that happened centuries ago around Lake Geneva
(A) In the sixth century Gregory of Tours, a chronicler* of the Germanic people known as the Franks, told of an extraordinary event in what is now Switzerland, where the Rhone River spills into Lake Geneva. He wrote of a big rockfall in the year 563 AD in the vicinity of a place called Tauredunum. The debris plunged into the river, and a great mass of water 'overwhelmed with a sudden and violent flood all that was on the banks as far as the city of Geneva,' more than 64 kilometres across the lake. The Geneva bridge was demolished, and several people inside the city walls of Geneva were killed. Historians and scientists have long believed that Gregory and another chronicler, Marius of Avenches, who told a similar tale, were describing a tsunami that raced across the lake. But there has not been any direct evidence of it until now.
 
(B) Researchers at the University of Geneva now say they have found that evidence, in the form of a large deposit of sediment in the middle of the lake. In a study published in the journal Nature Geoscience, they also propose the sequence of events that caused the deadly surge. The researchers think that large boulders crashed down onto soft sediments which had accumulated at the river mouth because of the slowing of the river's flow when it enters the lake. These sediments formed an underwater delta that had several canyon-like channels. When the falling rocks hit the delta they destabilised the sediments and caused the canyons to collapse. It was this collapse that created the tsunami. The sediments from this collapse would have been propelled towards the lake's centre.
 
(C) Guy Simpson, a lecturer in the University of Geneva's Department of Geology and Paleontology, says the thick layer of sediment, which has the same curved shape as a lens, lies more than 305 metres down in the deepest part of the lake, and was found largely by chance. Katrina Kremer, a University of Geneva doctoral student and the study's lead author, had been conducting seismic soundings, searching for thin sediment layers that might be evidence of major floods that had taken place in pre-historic times, long before the event described by Gregory of Tours. 'But we came across this enormous deposit,' Simpson says. 'We didn't know straight away that it was the deposit that caused the [sixth- century] tsunami. But it was a jumbled mess of sediment. It was quite obvious that it was deposited rapidly.'
 
(D) The researchers then took samples of the sediments and used carbon-dating techniques on remains of leaves and other organic matter they found to determine when the deposit formed. This narrowed the range to a period between the late fourth century and the early seventh century. Other than the rockfall, there is no record of any special event during that period, Simpson says.
 
(E) The researchers estimated that the deposit, which is at least 9.6 kilometres long by 4.8 kilometres wide, and averages about five metres thick, contains more than 248 million cubic metres of material. They ran multiple computer simulations showing that the collapse of that much sediment at the mouth of the Rhone would have caused a tsunami with an estimated height of 7.9 metres at Geneva - where it would have arrived in about 70 minutes. The rockfall itself may have been set off by a major earthquake, as some scientists have speculated.
 
(F) Lake tsunamis, although unusual, are not unknown, says Richard Schweickert, an Emeritus Professor of Geology at the University of Nevada in Reno, in the United States. He cites evidence that the collapse of part of the shoreline of Lake Tahoe in northern California within the past 20,000 years caused a tsunami with wave heights of about 30 metres. There are two faults under the lake that could have caused an earthquake, he says and that the collapse of the Rhone delta sediments, as calculated by the Swiss researchers, 'would certainly be capable of moving a large amount of material into the lake.' He suggests that the findings could be corroborated by careful mapping of the shoreline to look for unusual deposits or erosion left behind by the giant waves.
 
(G) Simpson says the Rhone delta sediments might collapse again, perhaps from an earthquake or even their own weight. In the sixth century, Geneva was a small community, mostly behind walls on a hill, whereas today it is home to international organisations and about 200,000 people, many living in low-lying areas near the water. Testing the stability of nearby slopes, and creating more detailed models of how a tsunami could affect Geneva today, would provide a more accurate assessment of whether or not this is something the lakeside city should be concerned about.
 
(H) Most tsunamis occur in oceans and are generated by earthquakes. However, the study is a reminder that even a landlocked nation like Switzerland is not immune to catastrophic waves.

Questions 1–7
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1–7 on your answer sheet, write.

Q1 According to Gregory of Tours, the landslide which caused the flood happened near Tauredunum.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q2 The city of Geneva was undamaged by the tsunami that Gregory described.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q3 The work of Marius of Avenches supported the idea that there was a tsunami.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q4 The rocks which fell into the delta were very hard and dense.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q5 Richard Schweickert has published studies on lake tsunamis that have occurred in several countries.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 The shoreline of Lake Tahoe has remained unchanged for 20,000 years.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q7 Parts of the population of Geneva now live closer to the lake than was the case in the sixth century.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

干扰 你可能会因为找不着“landslide”这个词而犹豫，但原文的“big rockfall”（大块岩石崩塌）就是指代滑坡的意思。

句子 (A) In the sixth century Gregory of Tours, a chronicler* of the Germanic people known as the Franks, told of an extraordinary event in what is now Switzerland, where the Rhone River spills into Lake Geneva. He wrote of a big rockfall in the year 563 AD in the vicinity of a place called Tauredunum. The debris plunged into the river, and a great mass of water 'overwhelmed with a sudden and violent flood all that was on the banks as far as the city of Geneva,' more than 64 kilometres across the lake.

解析 原文明确提到Gregory记录了一场发生在Tauredunum附近的大规模岩石崩塌（滑坡），并引发了洪水，这与题目描述完全一致，所以是TRUE。

Q2

解析 原文说日内瓦的桥梁被摧毁，城墙内的几个人也被杀了，这和题目说的“未受损（undamaged）”完全相反，所以是FALSE。

干扰 你可能没注意到“undamaged”这个带有否定前缀的词，把它当成了“受损”，从而导致误选TRUE。

句子 The debris plunged into the river, and a great mass of water 'overwhelmed with a sudden and violent flood all that was on the banks as far as the city of Geneva,' more than 64 kilometres across the lake. The Geneva bridge was demolished, and several people inside the city walls of Geneva were killed.

Q3

解析 原文提到另一位记录者Marius讲述了类似的故事，历史学家和科学家一直认为他们描述的就是一场海啸，这支持了题目的说法，所以是TRUE。

干扰 你可能没理解“told a similar tale”（讲了类似的故事）的意思，这其实就是指他支持了发生过海啸的观点。

句子 Historians and scientists have long believed that Gregory and another chronicler, Marius of Avenches, who told a similar tale, were describing a tsunami that raced across the lake.

Q4

干扰 你可能把修饰沉积物的“柔软（soft）”进行了反向推理，想当然地认为砸它的石头就一定是坚硬致密的，这是在过度脑补。

解析 原文只提到了大石头（large boulders）砸向了柔软的沉积物，根本没提这些石头本身是不是题目所说的“非常坚硬和致密（hard and dense）”，所以是NOT GIVEN。

句子 The researchers think that large boulders crashed down onto soft sediments which had accumulated at the river mouth because of the slowing of the river's flow when it enters the lake. These sediments formed an underwater delta that had several canyon-like channels.

Q5

解析 原文只提到Richard Schweickert引用了美国加州太浩湖的证据，根本没说他在“几个国家（several countries）”发表过关于湖泊海啸的研究，所以是NOT GIVEN。

干扰 你看到他是个教授且举了太浩湖的例子，可能就自己脑补他一定在很多国家做过调查并发表过文章，要记住做题不能凭空猜测。

句子 (F) Lake tsunamis, although unusual, are not unknown, says Richard Schweickert, an Emeritus Professor of Geology at the University of Nevada in Reno, in the United States. He cites evidence that the collapse of part of the shoreline of Lake Tahoe in northern California within the past 20,000 years caused a tsunami with wave heights of about 30 metres.

Q6

解析 原文说在过去的两万年里，太浩湖的部分海岸线发生了坍塌，这直接反驳了题目所说的“保持不变（unchanged）”，所以是FALSE。

干扰 你可能只定位到了20,000 years，没仔细看前面的collapse（坍塌），导致没有发现这其实是一个相互矛盾的信息。

句子 He cites evidence that the collapse of part of the shoreline of Lake Tahoe in northern California within the past 20,000 years caused a tsunami with wave heights of about 30 metres.

Q7

句子 In the sixth century, Geneva was a small community, mostly behind walls on a hill, whereas today it is home to international organisations and about 200,000 people, many living in low-lying areas near the water.

干扰 题目用了“closer to the lake than was the case in the sixth century”这种比较级句型，你可能没看懂这个“今昔对比”的表达。

解析 原文明确对比了日内瓦过去是在山上的城墙后，而今天很多人住在靠近水边的低洼地区，证明现在确实住得更近了，所以是TRUE。

Q8

解析 原文提到Katrina Kremer一直在寻找史前时期发生过的大洪水（major floods）的证据，所以填floods。

干扰 题目中的indications（迹象）对应原文的evidence（证据），如果你不知道这两个词是同义替换，就很难定位到floods。

句子 Katrina Kremer, a University of Geneva doctoral student and the study's lead author, had been conducting seismic soundings, searching for thin sediment layers that might be evidence of major floods that had taken place in pre-historic times, long before the event described by Gregory of Tours.

Q9

解析 原文明确说研究人员提取了沉积物样本，并对找到的树叶（leaves）和其他有机物质进行了碳年代测定，所以填leaves。

干扰 题目里的“such as”（例如）对应原文的“and other”（以及其他），找到这个并列关系就能直接填出leaves。

句子 (D) The researchers then took samples of the sediments and used carbon-dating techniques on remains of leaves and other organic matter they found to determine when the deposit formed.

Q10

句子 (D) The researchers then took samples of the sediments and used carbon-dating techniques on remains of leaves and other organic matter they found to determine when the deposit formed. This narrowed the range to a period between the late fourth century and the early seventh century.

解析 原文说碳测年技术把时间范围缩小到了4世纪末到7世纪（seventh century）初之间，所以填seventh。

干扰 题目说的是“beginning of the...”（……的初期），你要对应到原文的“early”（早期），千万不要看走眼填成fourth。

Q11

解析 原文说研究人员估计（estimated）了这个沉积物包含超过2.48亿立方米的物质，这指的就是测算体积（volume），所以填estimated。

干扰 你可能没意识到“contains more than 248 million cubic metres of material”就是在描述体积，所以找不到它对应的动词estimated。

句子 (E) The researchers estimated that the deposit, which is at least 9.6 kilometres long by 4.8 kilometres wide, and averages about five metres thick, contains more than 248 million cubic metres of material.

Q12

解析 原文说他们进行了多次计算机模拟，显示这场海啸在日内瓦的估计高度（height）为7.9米，并会在70分钟左右到达，所以填height。

干扰 题目里的“computer modelling”对应原文的“computer simulations”，只要找到计算机模拟的地方，就能发现它算出了高度和到达时间（speed）。

句子 They ran multiple computer simulations showing that the collapse of that much sediment at the mouth of the Rhone would have caused a tsunami with an estimated height of 7.9 metres at Geneva - where it would have arrived in about 70 minutes.

Q13

解析 原文直接指出，正如一些科学家推测的那样，岩石崩塌本身可能是由一场大地震（earthquake）引发的，所以填earthquake。

干扰 题目的“likely cause”（可能的原因）和“significant”（重大的）分别对应原文的“may have been set off by”（可能是由……引发）和“major”（主要的），理清这层替换关系就不会填错。

句子 The rockfall itself may have been set off by a major earthquake, as some scientists have speculated.
